uncited: It differs from its sibling [Task Shader Block-wise Stream Compaction](1540-task-shader-block-wise-stream-compaction.md) by performing the actual depth-based visibility test via rasterization rather than purely via compute-based occupancy checks, and from [GPU-driven Visibility Culling](3640-gpu-driven-visibility-culling.md) by relying on standard rasterization hardware for occlusion testing rather than ray tracing or other visibility acceleration structures.
The method operates in a pipeline involving task shaders, mesh shaders, rasterization, and compute shaders to filter voxel blocks.
This structure is passed to the mesh shader.
*   Generate a dense list of occupied blocks.
*   Utilize the **Representative Fragment Test** extension [KTB*18] if available.
*   **Multi-view Rendering:** When rendering per-eye, generate one quad per eye.
*   **Time Complexity:** The culling pass is dominated by the rasterization of proxy geometry.
The number of primitives is proportional to the number of potentially occupied blocks.
